item.title: U.S. Marshals capture fugitive wanted in Winston County shooting - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WINSTON COUNTY – A man wanted in connection with a shooting in Winston County and the attempted shooting of a law enforcement officer has been captured, according to the U.S. Marshals Service.

Bobby White Jr., 45, was arrested March 17 in Ackerman following a fugitive investigation led by the U.S. Marshals Service. White was wanted by the Winston County Sheriff’s Department on charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and attempted aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer.

Authorities said the case began March 12 after an adult male, believed to be a family member of White, was shot following an altercation on Miller Avenue in Louisville.

Emergency dispatchers received a call about the shooting, and as a Winston County sheriff’s deputy responded to the scene, officials said the suspect fired at the deputy. The deputy was not struck.

Investigators said the suspect then fled into the woods and was not immediately located. A warrant for White’s arrest was issued March 13.

On March 17, deputy U.S. marshals with the Gulf Coast Regional Fugitive Task Force tracked White to a home in the 1300 block of Concord-Bethsalem Road in Ackerman.

With assistance from the Winston County and Choctaw County sheriff’s departments, U.S. marshals surrounded the residence and took White into custody without incident.

item.title: Two charged after stolen vehicle recovered in Carroll County investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CARROLL COUNTY – Two men have been charged after deputies recovered a vehicle stolen from a senior citizen earlier this week, according to Carroll County officials.

Authorities said the Carroll County Emergency Operations Center received a call Monday morning, March 16, from a senior citizen who discovered her only mode of transportation had been stolen. Deputies were dispatched to a residence near the Greenwood Leflore Airport.

Investigators determined the vehicle had been taken during storms that moved through the area Sunday night.

Through the investigation, deputies developed suspects and, over the next 48 hours, worked with the Greenwood Police Department and the Tallahatchie County Sheriff’s Department to locate the vehicle.

The car was eventually recovered in Tallahatchie County.

Billy Earl Akins, 38, of Carrollton, and Edward Earl Henley, 33, of Greenwood, have been charged with theft of a motor vehicle. Akins remains jailed at the Carroll County Regional Correctional Facility.

Sheriff Clint Walker said cases involving senior citizens are a priority for his office.

“While we work for all the citizens of our county, there is a certain urgency when it comes to our senior citizens being victimized,” Walker said. “Many of them are on fixed incomes and rely on their vehicles to maintain their independence and mobility. We don’t rest until those who prey on them are held accountable.”

Walker also credited the cooperation between agencies for the quick recovery of the vehicle.

item.title: Saltillo man arrested after search warrant leads to meth, firearm seizure - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
SALTILLO – A Saltillo man was arrested after agents executing a search warrant found a felony amount of methamphetamine and numerous firearms at a home in the city, according to the Tupelo Police Department.

Authorities said agents with the North Mississippi Narcotics Unit and the Saltillo Police Department executed the search warrant March 6 at a residence on Pulltight Road in Saltillo.

During the search, investigators found a felony amount of suspected methamphetamine along with numerous firearms, officials said.

William Wallace Ellis, 53, of Saltillo, was arrested and charged with possession of a Schedule II controlled substance.

Lee County Justice Court Judge Chuck Hopkins set Ellis’ bond at $50,000.

Authorities said the case will be presented to the Lee County Grand Jury.

item.title: Pike County Sheriff’s Office adds analyst to ICAC Task Force to combat online child exploitation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PIKE COUNTY – The Pike County Sheriff’s Office has added a new member to assist in the fight against online child exploitation through its partnership with the Mississippi Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, according to Sheriff Bryant “Wally” Jones.

Officials said Intelligence Analyst Aaron Adams joined the ICAC Task Force as an affiliate member on Monday, March 16.

The ICAC Unit, operated by the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office, is responsible for investigating online child exploitation cases across the state.

Adams joins Lt. Det. Javonda Shanks of the Pike County Sheriff’s Office, who has served as an affiliate member of the task force since 2024. Former Pike County Sheriff’s Office detectives Matthew Travis and Max Adams also serve as full-time members of the ICAC Task Force under the Attorney General’s Office.

Sheriff Jones said the addition strengthens the county’s ongoing efforts to protect children and support statewide investigations.

“I’m proud of Aaron and all of the ICAC members who help keep our communities safe from child predators,” Jones said. “He will be a great addition to the unit and brings a lot of talent to the table. We will continue to partner with the Mississippi Attorney General and the ICAC Unit for years to come.”

The sheriff’s office said the partnership reflects its continued commitment to combating online child exploitation and enhancing public safety.

item.title: One airlifted after overturned vehicle crash on Highway 61 South in Coahoma County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COAHOMA COUNTY – Emergency crews responded to an overturned vehicle late Tuesday night in Coahoma County, where one person was seriously injured.

According to the Coahoma County Fire Department, units were dispatched at approximately 11:32 p.m. to the area of Highway 61 South for a report of a crash involving an overturned vehicle.

Upon arrival, firefighters found an individual outside the vehicle with severe traumatic injuries. Paramedics provided immediate medical treatment before the person was airlifted to a regional trauma center.

Firefighters from Lyon, Lula and Jonestown assisted at the scene, along with Pafford EMS.

The Mississippi Highway Patrol is investigating the incident.

item.title: Natchez to host program on Indigenous language revitalization, annual powwow later this month - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NATCHEZ – A public program highlighting the history and revitalization of the Indigenous Natchez language will be held later this month, followed by the city’s annual Natchez Powwow, according to event organizers.

The language program is scheduled for Wednesday, March 26, at 6 p.m. at the Grand Village of the Natchez Indians. The event will feature Dr. Geoffrey Kimball, author of Natchez Analytical Dictionary, who will discuss the last fluent speakers of the Natchez language and early 20th-century efforts to document it.

Dr. Keith Cunningham will also speak about how the newly published dictionary is being used to help descendants of the Natchez people develop educational tools aimed at reviving the language.

Relatives of the last fluent speakers from the Sam family are expected to attend and share their genealogy and ongoing preservation efforts.

Following the program, attendees will have the opportunity to meet Kimball during a book signing. Copies of the dictionary will be available for purchase. The event is free and open to the public, and refreshments will be provided.

“The Natchez language is an important part of the history of this region,” said Roscoe Barnes, cultural heritage and tourism manager for Visit Natchez. “Programs like this allow residents and visitors to learn more about the people and stories connected to Natchez while supporting efforts to document and revitalize the language for future generations.”

Later in the week, the Natchez Powwow will take place March 28–29 on the Natchez Bluff at 319 N. Broadway St. The annual event will feature Native American dancers, singers, artisans and vendors from across the region.

Organizers said the family-friendly event will include traditional dance exhibitions, music, arts and crafts, and food vendors. Admission is free.

“This is a wholesome family event that provides good entertainment and a celebration of Native American culture in a safe environment,” said Natchez Powwow Chairman Dr. Chuck Borum. “We invite everyone to come enjoy themselves.”

Oscar-nominated songwriter Scott George, known for “Wahzhazhe (A Song for My People)” from Killers of the Flower Moon, is expected to participate in this year’s powwow, along with Eddie Yellowfish, who will serve as head singer of the Southern Drum.

Organizers encourage attendees to bring lawn chairs for seating.

For more information, visit natchezpowwow.com.

item.title: Missing Covington County man found dead in Mississippi River after weeks long search - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – The Adams County Sheriff’s Office says a missing man who was originally reported out of Covington County has been found dead after an extensive multi-agency search.

According to the sheriff’s office, Cornelius Elijah Allen, 31, was located deceased in the Mississippi River near the Hydro Plant on Highway 15 in Louisiana, about an hour from Vidalia.

Authorities said Allen was identified through personal identification found on his body. The Natchez Police Department, which has been leading the investigation, confirmed the discovery. Family members have been notified.

Allen was originally reported missing Feb. 25, 2026.

UPDATE: Missing man’s vehicle found abandoned near Natchez riverfront

His body was found after weeks of coordinated search efforts involving the Adams County Search and Rescue Team, the Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks, the Adams County Sheriff’s Office, the Natchez Police Department and the Concordia Parish Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff Travis Patten and the Adams County Sheriff’s Office thanked the agencies, volunteers and community members who assisted in the search.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with Mr. Allen’s family during this incredibly difficult time,” Patten said. “We ask the community to continue to lift them up in prayer as they seek comfort and closure.”

The Adams County Sheriff’s Office said it will continue assisting the Natchez Police Department and partner agencies as the investigation continues.

item.title: Jackson State to host national teacher recruitment fair amid ongoing educator shortage - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Jackson State University will host a national teacher recruitment fair this week as part of efforts to address ongoing educator shortages in Mississippi and across the country, according to a university press release.

The JSU Career Services Center will hold the 2026 Teacher Recruitment Fair on Thursday, March 19, from 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. in the Terry L. Woodard Ballroom on the third floor of the Student Center. The event is open to all majors and alumni, with opportunities for placement in K-12 classrooms.

“The Career Services Center has a long collaborative history with hosting this event for our education majors,” said Lashanda W. Jordan, executive director of JSU Career and Student Services. “We believe this event is important in assisting our students with launching their careers in the field of education.”

University officials said approximately 55 school districts from across the country are expected to participate, along with organizations such as Black Men Teach and Teachers Like Me, which focus on recruiting and supporting educators.

Jordan said the event allows Jackson State to connect its graduates with districts seeking qualified teachers and to highlight the university’s education programs on a national level.

The recruitment effort comes as Mississippi continues to face a significant teacher shortage. According to the Mississippi Department of Education, the state reported more than 6,000 vacancies for teachers, administrators and support staff based on a survey conducted between August and November 2025.

Officials have cited low pay, burnout and limited benefits as contributing factors. The largest shortages are in math, science and special education.

State lawmakers are currently working to reconcile competing proposals for teacher pay raises. The Mississippi Senate has approved a plan that would provide a $6,000 raise for teachers and an additional $3,000 for special education teachers, while the House has passed a plan offering a $5,000 raise phased in over three years.

Nationwide, a report from the Learning Policy Institute found nearly 46,000 unfilled teaching positions across 31 states and the District of Columbia.

University officials said the recruitment fair is an opportunity to help fill gaps while positioning Jackson State as a leading source of educators in Mississippi and beyond.

“The JSU Teacher Recruitment Day provides us the opportunity to showcase our talented students and ensure school districts across not only the state of Mississippi but the country know that our program is top-notch,” Jordan said.

item.title: Hinds County Sheriff’s Office to unveil monument honoring fallen deputies and jailers - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HINDS COUNTY – The Hinds County Sheriff’s Office will host a ceremony next week to unveil a monument honoring deputies and jailers who died in the line of duty.

The Fallen Deputies and Jailers Monument Unveiling Ceremony is scheduled for Thursday, March 19, at 10 a.m. at the Hinds County Sheriff’s Office headquarters, located at 407 E. Pascagoula St. in Jackson.

According to the sheriff’s office, the monument will honor the lives, service and sacrifice of deputies and jailers who gave their lives while serving the citizens of Hinds County.

Officials said the monument is intended to serve as a lasting tribute to their courage, dedication and commitment to protecting the community.

The event is free and open to the public. Community members are encouraged to attend as the sheriff’s office joins families of the fallen and public safety partners in remembering those who made the ultimate sacrifice.

The sheriff’s office also issued a traffic advisory for the morning of the ceremony. Tombigbee Street will be temporarily closed from 7 a.m. until about 11 a.m. at the intersections of State Street and Tombigbee Street, Congress Street and Tombigbee Street, and President Street and Tombigbee Street.

item.title: "He gave me the creeps": Victim's neighbor testifies about meeting Tellis - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — Katelyn Hearn remembers the day that she met the man she identified on Wednesday as Quinton Tellis, telling the court that “he creeped me out” enough that she went inside and locked the door.

Hearn testified on Day 3 of the murder trial of Tellis in the 2015 death of Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao in Monroe, Louisiana. Tellis, who remains the main suspect in the 2014 burning death of Jessica Chambers in Courtland, Mississippi, is alleged to have killed Hsiao less than 10 months after Chambers’ death.

Prosecutors used Hearn’s testimony to help draw out a timeline of when Tellis was at Hsiao’s apartment in the days leading up to her death.

Hearn said Hsiao had visitors from time to time, including a woman in a gold vehicle. But she had only seen the black Impala registered to Tellis’s then-fiancee Chakita Jackson within the week of Hsiao’s death. The first time she saw it, she told the court, was on July 27, 2015.

READ: Tellis trial, Day 1: Interview videos

She had been asleep, Hearn testified, when she heard someone knock on the door, and then heard footsteps retreating down the metal stairs outside her upstairs apartment. Thinking it was a package being delivered, she went to the door, where she found a child. Hearn said the child asked her, “Do you know where that white lady that lives downstairs is?”

Hearn told him no, then looked down the stairs to see an adult man standing by Hsiao’s bike and a young teenager standing by the Impala. The man she identified in court as Tellis struck up a conversation, asking her if she knew where Hsiao was. He ended up asking her,”Do you have a baby inside?”

The question was strange, Hearn thought, and she testified that “red flags went up.” She told the judge that she has an almost photographic memory, and it’s heightened when she has an extreme reaction to things. She testified that the fear that she felt sharpened her memory of Tellis, particularly his face. When she identified him in a photo lineup after Hsiao’s body was found, she remembered him clearly.

The black car would come back twice more that day, once after Hsiao came home, and then again that evening. On the second visit, she didn’t see Tellis, but she saw the two children from before playing in the yard. Given that she had been afraid the last time he was there, Hearn called her boyfriend and asked him to come home for lunch. When he left, Hearn asked him to get the license plate of the black Impala. She said she often gets the license numbers of strange vehicles.

RELATED: Tellis trial, Day 2: The crime scene

On the third time she saw the vehicle that day, she heard a voice she remembered as belonging to the man she identified as Tellis from the conversation that morning and he seemed to be arguing with Hsiao. Defense attorney Randy Donald asked her on cross examination about a statement she had made about Hsiao being a loud talker, in case it wasn’t an actual argument.

“She was a loud talker, but I could tell her voice was raised,” Hearn said. She testified that even when Hsiao had company, she could never hear the conversations, except occasionally when they laughed loudly.

On the night of July 29, Hearn testified that she and her boyfriend had been out and came home around dusk. When they pulled in, they could tell that Hsiao’s lights were off, but her bike was outside. Hearn said she noted that because usually when they pulled in, they could see into her apartment because the lights were on. She noted that for some reason, the apartment being dark “creeped me out again.”

As they prepared dinner, Hearn went into her bedroom to change clothes. She heard a noise come from downstairs that sounded like the bed falling off the frame, a problem she had with her bed in the pre-furnished apartment that exactly mirrored Hsiao’s. She mentioned to her boyfriend that it sounded like “Mandy’s having the same problem with her bed that we have.”

Hearn said the problem with the bed frame was one that was frequent. She said it would fall of sometimes just when she would roll over in her sleep.

“Sometimes even just if you sat down on the bed to tie your shoe,” she said.

item.title: Texas woman killed after two vehicles hit detached trailer in Covington County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COVINGTON COUNTY – A Texas woman was killed Monday morning in a three-vehicle crash involving a detached tractor-trailer on U.S. Highway 49, according to the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

The crash occurred around 5:06 a.m. on March 16.

Authorities said a 2016 Volvo tractor-trailer driven by Filmon T. Abraha, 29, of Garland, Texas, was traveling south when it briefly left the roadway and then re-entered. When the vehicle returned to the roadway, the second trailer became detached.

A 2013 Nissan Altima driven by Lyle B. Wheat, 30, of Collins, was also traveling south when it collided with the detached trailer in the roadway. A 2026 Kia Sportage driven by Arlene I. Turner, 67, of San Antonio, Texas, then also struck the trailer.

Officials said Abraha and Wheat were not injured in the crash.

Turner sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by the Covington County Coroner’s Office.

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: Quinton Tellis trial, Day 2: Detective describes Mandy Hsiao's death scene - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — When dispatch alerted Sgt. Duane Cookson of the situation on Filihol Road, he only knew he was headed to a deceased female.

There was decomposition, he was told, and foul odor. When he got there, what he found told a grim story of brutality that investigators have talked about in the time that’s passed as one of the most brutal scenes they’ve come across.

Cookson took the stand on Tuesday in the trial of Quinton Tellis in Monroe, Louisiana. Tellis is accused in the 2015 stabbing death of Ming Chen Hsiao, known to her friends as Mandy.

Both the prosecution and the defense laid out their opening statements Tuesday morning, with Assistant District Attorney Holly Jones painting a picture of Tellis as a soulless, calculating killer who tortured Hsiao to death to get the pin number for her debit card, and the defense contending that there would be absolutely no evidence that would stand to show Tellis had killed her.

Jones said cell phone records, both locational and call logs, would show Tellis was with Hsiao when she died, and that he dialed her bank and entered her credit card information, including the pin, twice from her phone and once from his just moments after she allegedly died. Defense attorney Randall Donald said the defense would rely on the inaccuracy of phone records to show that there’s no proof that Tellis caused Hsiao’s death.

Whoever did it, though, left a scene that disturbed Cookson in 2015 and those in the courtroom Tuesday when he was called to testify as the state’s first witness.

Hsiao had been dead at least a week when she was found, according to investigators. Photos shown by the prosecution as Cookson testified Tuesday showed some of her 30 stab wounds in advanced decomposition. Her 5’3″, 100 lb frame lay half face down, half sideways at the foot of her bed, with her head partly under the footboard.

Blood spatter adorned the bed, the walls, the doors, and a suitcase, and Cookson said the odor of decomposition could be smelled at least 20 feet away from the apartment when he arrived. A neighbor had called the landlord after seeing flies by the door and noticing the smell, Cookson testified, and the landlord had alerted police from a call box across the street.

Photos submitted into evidence by the prosecution showed Hsiao’s door standing open, and even as soon as the photographer stepped in the door, her body could be seen in the bedroom down the hall.

During the showing of the photos, Tellis’ face was emotionless. He sat with his hands and feet shackled, wearing his prison jumpsuit, and watched with a blank expression.

The TV Tellis alleged he had bought from Hsiao sat on a TV stand in the living room, and the counters and table were covered with signs of life — basic clutter, cleaning products, hair accessories, and the like. Her wallet was on the bed, her phone was on the floor, and her Chase bank card was nowhere to be found, according to the prosecution.

There was a bloody print — possibly a palm print — with a ridged pattern on one of the doors, but there didn’t seem to be footprints or any other direct evidence of the killer. Cookson testified that with the advanced decomposition, it was fairly clear they were dealing with a homicide, but either way it was obviously a suspicious death.

The bed was off the frame, the slats having come loose and the box spring had fallen in part to the floor. In the opening statements, Jones had told the judge that the neighbor upstairs had heard a noise that sounded like the box springs falling off the frame. She had laid out a timeline that showed that Hsiao had messaged with a friend at 7:41 that night and that the calls had been made to the bank from her phone and Tellis’s at 8:16. During that time frame, Jones said, is when Tellis allegedly killed her, and cell phone data will put him in the area of the apartment.

Jones said Mohammed Mahrouz will testify that Tellis gave him Hsiao’s card and told him to go get money off of it at Chase Bank. When he got there, he was afraid, so he just got a bank balance and came back. Eric Hill, the cousin of Tellis’s then-wife Chakita Jackson, will testify that Tellis threatened him to find a fall guy for the killing or “he’d do to him what he did to that girl.” Hill allegedly framed a man named Curtis Lemons, who detectives found to have an alibi. Hill will testify in court this week, Jones said, that the reason he knew details of the killing that only the killer could know was because Tellis told him about it.

Donald told the judge that the DNA at the scene excludes Tellis. In previous reporting, it has come out that Hsiao’s level of decomposition had made it impossible to identify any DNA besides hers, but it’s unclear if there has been more evidence since then.

The defense agreed that Tellis had pleaded guilty around a decade ago to charges of using Hsiao’s debit card, but Donald asserted that it doesn’t mean that Tellis killed her. Donald referred to Hsiao as “this young lady,” but never said her name.

Tellis is also the main suspect in the 2014 burning death of Jessica Chambers in Panola County, Mississippi. If the prosecution’s timeline is correct, Tellis allegedly killed Chambers, moved to Monroe to be with his fiancee, then allegedly killed Hsiao about eight months later before he was a clear suspect in the Chambers killing. When he was indicted in Mississippi, he was in jail in Ouachita Parish in connection with Hsiao’s death.

Judge Larry Jefferson dismissed court for lunch around 12:15 p.m. Court resumes at 1:30 p.m.

Organizers encourage residents to stop by, donate blood and help support patients in need while enjoying food and entertainment.

item.title: Man pleads guilty to federal firearm charge in North Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
GREENVILLE — A man has pleaded guilty in federal court to illegally possessing firearms following his arrest along the Natchez Trace Parkway in North Mississippi, authorities said.

According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Mississippi, Daniel Mireles-Reyna entered the guilty plea before Debra M. Brown. He faces a maximum sentence of 15 years in prison, with sentencing set for a later date.

Court documents show Mireles-Reyna was arrested Dec. 26, 2025, on the Natchez Trace Parkway near Tupelo.

Law enforcement rangers with the National Park Service responded to the scene and discovered Mireles-Reyna had a loaded stolen handgun in his pocket. Authorities said a search of his vehicle uncovered two additional firearms, including a Glock handgun and a Draco 7.62 firearm, along with ammunition and suspected narcotics.

During the investigation, agents with Homeland Security Investigations determined Mireles-Reyna was not a U.S. citizen and was in the country unlawfully after entering from Mexico.

Officials said the case was investigated by the National Park Service and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney John Herzog Jr. is prosecuting the case.

The case is part of a federal initiative known as Operation Take Back America, which focuses on addressing violent crime and transnational criminal activity.

item.title: Human remains discovered in Claiborne County; MBI investigating - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLAIBORNE COUNTY – The Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office is investigating the discovery of human remains found within the county, according to Sheriff Edward L. Goods Sr.

Because of the nature of the discovery and the condition of the remains, the case has been turned over to the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation for further examination and assistance.

Authorities said the remains have not been positively identified.

Investigators also said the body was discovered in a decomposed state, making it impossible at this time to immediately determine the cause of death. As a result, foul play has not been ruled out.

The Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office said it will continue working closely with the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation and other appropriate agencies to determine the identity of the individual and the circumstances surrounding the case.

Officials are asking anyone with information that could assist investigators to contact the Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office.

The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Free health talks to focus on kidney-heart connection during Kidney Awareness Month - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MADISON – A series of free community health talks aimed at raising awareness about the connection between kidney and heart health will be held in central Mississippi during March, which is recognized as Kidney Awareness Month.

Health by Brick announced it will host the interactive discussions at locations including libraries and cafés across the area. The events are designed to help participants better understand the science-backed relationship between kidney and heart health.

Organizers say the talks will begin with a “Pre-Talk Huddle,” which will include a rapid health screening, several short exercises focused on improving overall health and an opportunity for attendees to ask questions directly to a health professional.

The main presentation will focus on practical ways people can prioritize their health and better understand how the heart and kidneys work together to support the body.

The events are free to attend, but organizers say space is limited and advance registration is encouraged.

People interested in attending can select a location and register online at healthbybrick.com/events.

The talks will be held in communities including Jackson, Madison and Pearl.

item.title: Defendant to be transferred to federal custody following plea in Walthall County case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WALTHALL COUNTY – A defendant in a child-related case will be transferred to federal custody following the resolution of charges in Walthall County Circuit Court, according to District Attorney Brendon Adams.

Edwin Rigoberto Orocco Ramirez, who had been held in the Walthall County Jail, entered a plea to one count of touching a child for lustful purposes. He received a 15-year sentence, which was suspended.

Officials said the sentence was structured to allow for Ramirez to be promptly transferred into the custody of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement so that federal immigration proceedings can move forward without delay.

Adams said the resolution of the state case was handled in coordination with a federal warrant to ensure accountability under federal immigration law.

“Our office works diligently to be good stewards of local, state and federal resources to ensure that justice is served and defendants are held accountable for their crimes,” Adams said. “Though sentences may seem unique at times, our office operates strategically and tactically to ensure that our communities remain safe for our families to live, work and worship.”

Authorities also commended the witnesses, officers and investigators involved in the case.

item.title: Trial begins today for Quinton Tellis in 2015 killing of Taiwanese exchange student - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, Louisiana — The murder trial for Quinton Tellis is happening today in Monroe, Louisiana after being rescheduled multiple times. This case has stretched on for nearly a decade.

Tellis is charged in Ouachita Parish with first-degree murder in the 2015 death of 34-year-old Meng-Chen Hsiao, a Taiwanese exchange student who was found tortured to death in Monroe, Louisiana.

The trial has been set to begin several times, most recently being postponed in December after the death of key expert witness Brigadier General Paul Rowlett, then again in January when ADA Holly Jones had the flue. Earlier this month, the trial was postponed again by the winter storm.

Tellis, 36, has long maintained his innocence in Hsiao’s death. Prosecutors allege he killed Hsiao in order to take her debit card. He pleaded guilty to using her card after he was caught on ATM cameras in Vicksburg.

The case has drawn national attention because Tellis was also charged in Mississippi with the 2014 burning death of Jessica Chambers in Panola County. He was tried twice in that case, but both trials ended in mistrials due to hung juries. It is unclear if he will be tried again by the state of Mississippi.

If convicted, Tellis could face a sentence of life in prison or the death penalty.

The proceedings are expected to take place in Ouachita Parish District Court.

item.title: Tree falls on Natchez home during overnight storm, trapping occupants inside - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
NATCHEZ – A large tree fell onto a home in Natchez late Saturday night, causing major damage and temporarily trapping the occupants inside, according to the Adams County Sheriff’s Office.

Deputies said the incident happened around 11:30 p.m. March 15 in the 70 block of Mullins Road after a 911 caller reported that a tree had fallen onto the residence.

The caller told dispatchers the damage was significant and that the people inside could not safely get out of the home, authorities said.

When deputies arrived, they found that a large tree had fallen across the structure, causing structural damage and blocking access to the residence.

The Natchez Fire Department and AMR also responded to assist.

Emergency crews worked to secure the scene, help the occupants and assess the damage to the home. Officials said no serious injuries were reported.

The Adams County Sheriff’s Office reminded residents to use caution after severe weather, noting that fallen trees and debris can create dangerous conditions.

item.title: STEPPING UP TO SERVE: Deputies help rescue dog trapped after tree crushes car in Natchez - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ADAMS COUNTY – Some heroes wear capes, but today’s heroes wear badges. They went above and beyond in a situation where they didn’t have to.

According to the Adams County Sheriff, a large tree fell onto a parked vehicle early Monday morning in Natchez, trapping a puppy underneath.

Deputies said they were called around 12:35 a.m. March 16 to a home in the 1500 block of Martin Luther King Jr. Street.

A 911 call was received reporting that a tree had fallen onto a vehicle in the yard of the home.

When deputies arrived, they found a large oak tree resting on top of a parked vehicle. The vehicle appeared to be disabled and was unoccupied at the time of the incident.

The caller also reported that a puppy had become trapped underneath the vehicle due to the weight of the tree pressing down on the car.

Deputies and responding personnel worked tirelessly to help to assess the situation and assist with efforts to safely remove the tree and free the terrified pup.

Thanks to the quick work of the Adams County deputies, nobody was injured. What could have been a terrible situation ended in a positive way.

Officials reminded residents to remain cautious following severe weather, noting that fallen trees and debris can create dangerous conditions for both people and property.

We are thankful for those who have compassion and choose to help even when it’s beyond their job description. These deputies are heroes and this family and the sweet puppy were definitely thankful.

item.title: Shaw Pit Bull Rescue seeks sponsors to help feed 23 dogs through March - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COLUMBUS – Shaw Pit Bull Rescue is asking for the public’s help covering the cost of food for the dogs in its care this month.

The cost to sponsor one day of food is $48, which covers one full bag of food for all 23 dogs for that day.

The rescue said it uses Fromm Adult Gold dog food, which is available through Four Seasons Farm & Garden in Columbus. Supporters can donate a bag by calling the store at 662-329-2281 and designating it for Shaw Pit Bull Rescue.

Officials said the following days in March still need sponsors: March 3, 6, 8, 12, 14, 17, 19, 22, 25, 27, 29 and 31.

The rescue thanked the community for helping keep the dogs fed, healthy and cared for.

item.title: Rankin County deputies seize more than 2,000 kratom packets during investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office has seized more than 2,000 packets of kratom from convenience stores following an investigation into the sale of the substance in unincorporated areas of the county.

According to the sheriff’s office, the investigation began after citizens reported complaints about kratom being sold at local convenience stores.

In March 2024, the Rankin County Board of Supervisors passed a county ordinance prohibiting the use, purchase, possession, distribution, sale or offering for sale of synthetic cocaine and kratom in unincorporated areas of Rankin County.

After the ordinance was approved, deputies hand-delivered copies of the new law to convenience stores across the county.

Investigators later conducted undercover purchases and audits of stores located in unincorporated areas of Rankin County.

The operation resulted in the seizure of approximately 2,030 packets of kratom, with an estimated value of $48,267.12, according to the sheriff’s office.

Store employees who allegedly sold kratom to undercover agents have been charged with violating the county ordinance. The violation carries a penalty of up to $1,000 in fines and/or up to six months in the county jail.

Authorities said the seized kratom products will be held as evidence until the cases are resolved and will then be destroyed.

The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office encourages residents to report stores selling illegal products in the county by calling 601-825-1480.

item.title: Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department introduces bloodhound trained for search and recovery - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – The Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department has introduced a new four-legged member of its team, a bloodhound trained to help locate missing persons and fugitives.

Amos, a 3-year-old bloodhound, has been trained in tracking and finding missing people as well as fugitive recovery, according to the sheriff’s department.

Officials said Capt. Shane Edgar traveled to Missouri to meet Amos and complete four days of training with him before bringing the dog back to Pearl River County. Since then, Amos has continued training in the county’s climate and terrain to prepare for local conditions, including heat, humidity and varied environments.

The sheriff’s department said Amos has already completed multiple successful tracks in a variety of locations and weather conditions.

Authorities said they are confident in Amos’ ability to work alongside deputies, the department’s Special Operations Team and Pearl River County JSAR.

Officials said Amos is expected to strengthen the department’s search and recovery efforts and improve its ability to support nearby and local agencies.

item.title: Operation Check Mate leads to 30 arrests, drug and firearm seizures in Meridian - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MERIDIAN – Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced the completion of Operation Check Mate, a multi-agency law enforcement effort led by the Attorney General’s Office Fentanyl Strike Force.

According to Fitch’s office, the operation resulted in 20 felony arrests, 10 misdemeanor arrests, one DUI, 156 traffic citations and the execution of one search warrant.

“Fighting the fentanyl epidemic cannot be done without cooperation. It takes all of us,” Fitch said in a statement. “My office is committed to building a network of law enforcement across the state with the tools and knowledge to disrupt drug operations and successfully prosecute these criminals. Thank you to our local, state and federal partners who worked with us during this operation. Together, we can get these dangerous criminals out of our communities and drugs off of our streets.”

During the operation, law enforcement officers seized four firearms, marijuana, methamphetamine, MDMA pills, crack cocaine, suspected fentanyl powder, $7,368 in suspected illicit proceeds and 40 illegal gambling devices.

Participating agencies included the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Lauderdale County Sheriff’s Department, the Meridian Police Department, Mississippi Alcoholic Beverage Control, the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics, the Mississippi Gaming Commission and the Naval Criminal Investigative Service.

Fitch created the Fentanyl Strike Force in 2023 as part of the rollout of the One Pill Can Kill public education and awareness campaign.

Officials said Operation Check Mate followed one of the free Fentanyl Strike Force training sessions offered by the Attorney General’s Office. More than 800 officers have now been trained in narcotics investigations, as well as in the use of naloxone and fentanyl test strips.

Law enforcement agencies interested in participating in the Fentanyl Strike Force can contact the Attorney General’s Office at [email protected] .
